text.p: Malawi's ruling party failed to obtain a parliamentary quorum on Monday in the absence of two opposition parties which have been boycotting the National Assembly for months now.

The ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) has only 84 seats in the 177-seat assembly. Under the country's constitution, the parliament must have 118 members for a quorum on the first day of a new session.

The opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) have boycotted the house since July in protest at President Bakili Muluzi's appointment of five opposition members into his cabinet, without consulting their own parties.

National Assembly Speaker Rodwell Munyenyembe was visibly irate over the opposition's boycott of the house on Monday. He said their absence without authority demeaned the integrity and dignity of parliament.
"Absence denies any community good governance through parliament. We are legislators with power to determine the means for achieving the wishes of Malawians in the best way possible," he added.
But AFORD national chairman Chipimpha Mughogho told reporters there would not be a change of heart.
"We have made our position clear that we can not go back to parliament until our case is resolved," he said.

Former Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Rolf Patel, who pulled out of the ruling UDF party in August to stand as an independent MP, called for the house to adjourn because of the failure to reach a two-thirds majority.
"We are the people who make the laws of the country. I find it appalling that we must be the first ones to break the law.

"If we want to flout the law, we must make it clear that we're breaking the law. The law is the law, and there is no quorum in this house," Patel argued from an empty opposition bench which had only six members.
Munyenyembe however said the house would sit, adding:
"Parliament is not a play thing -- Parliament has to be taken seriously because it will outlive us and our private purposes, and therefore it should be respected for that reason."
The opposition MCP has threatened legal action to stop parliament sitting without a quorum, but has not indicated when court papers are to be lodged.
